title: Repair the Roof or Replace It
description: One cracked boot is a repair. A slope of bruised mats, a soft deck, or a discontinued shingle is a replacement. Here is how we sort them.
html:
The expensive mistake is replacing a roof that needed a boot. The expensive mistake the other way is patching a roof whose mat is already broken, then paying for the ceiling anyway. We try not to sell you either one.

Repair is the right job when

  • The leak traces to one boot, one flashing, or a short run of valley.
  • The surrounding shingles still have granules, lie flat, and match something we can buy.
  • The deck under that spot is solid when you walk it.
  • Hail hit a handful of tabs, not the whole exposure.

That is roof repair. We fix the detail, replace the damaged courses, and leave the rest of a sound roof alone.

Replacement is the right job when

  • Bruises cover a slope, or more than one slope, and the mat is soft.
  • The deck is spongy, stained through, or has been patched in layers.
  • There are already two roofs on the house. A third layer is a bad idea in this heat, and many cities will not allow it.
  • The shingle is discontinued, so every repair will be a color scar.
  • You have paid for the same valley twice.

A bundle that says 30 years does not mean 30 Texas summers. Heat and hail spend that label faster than a mild climate does. Fifteen to twenty hard years is a common place to start the replacement conversation. It is not a rule. The roof in front of us decides.

What a replacement week looks like

Once materials are on site and the weather holds, a typical house is one to three days on the roof: tear-off, dry-in, and install. The suburb replacement timeline is the day-by-day version for Tomball, Cypress, and The Woodlands. If you are weighing a patch against a roof replacement, request a free inspection. We will tell you which one we would put on our own house. (281) 541-0027.
